rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a material policy-letter template: both communications address Congress about corporation-tax policy, reaffirm an Administration position against near-term rate reductions, and expressly condition future fiscal action on the budgetary and developing economic outlook. C15 has a similar revenue-preservation rationale but is a veto memorandum focused on selective industry relief. C18 shares the form of a congressional appeal tied to a Budget Message, but its substantive machinery is unrelated.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Budget Message in January recommended a continuation, without change, of the corporation income tax and excise tax rates
shared_material.parent_excerpt: no action should be taken by the Congress at this time which will involve any substantial tax reduction for anyone
shared_material.explanation: Both state a near-term Administration policy of preserving existing tax rates and ask Congress to act consistently with it.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Consideration of fiscal measures will continue to be made in the light of the developing economic situation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to the existence of appropriate budgetary conditions ... In the economic conditions that prevail currently and can be expected during the next fiscal year
shared_material.explanation: Both reserve future tax-policy decisions for reassessment in light of changing economic and budgetary conditions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: after consultation by the Secretary of the Treasury with leaders of both political parties in the Congress
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Congress should, however, in connection with its study ... appropriately consider some of the other suggestions
shared_material.explanation: Both use a presidential letter to frame tax recommendations as matters for congressional consideration, although the later letter adds explicit bipartisan consultation.
